description.summary: pgvector is an open-source PostgreSQL extension for storing vectors and performing exact or approximate vector similarity search.
description.description: pgvector adds vector data types, distance operators, exact nearest-neighbor search, and HNSW or IVFFlat approximate indexes to PostgreSQL. It can participate in SQL filtering, PostgreSQL full-text hybrid retrieval, transactions, replication, backup, and operational tooling provided by the PostgreSQL ecosystem. This record distinguishes extension-native capabilities from host-database and deployment-dependent behavior.

indexingConsiderations: Use exact search when perfect recall is required; introduce HNSW or IVFFlat only after measuring the acceptable recall-speed tradeoff.
Create and tune a separate operator-class index for each distance function used by production queries.
Build approximate indexes after loading representative data, and monitor build memory, build time, and recall.
retrievalConsiderations: Compare approximate results with exact search and tune hnsw.ef_search, ivfflat.probes, or iterative-scan limits.
Treat approximate filtering as planner- and configuration-dependent; consider scalar indexes, partial vector indexes, partitioning, or iterative scans.
Implement hybrid retrieval by combining pgvector results with PostgreSQL full-text search and an explicit fusion or reranking strategy.

limitations: HNSW and IVFFlat trade exact recall for query speed and require workload-specific tuning.
HNSW generally uses more memory and builds more slowly, while IVFFlat requires representative data and list/probe tuning.
Approximate-index filtering is applied after the vector index scan by default and can return fewer rows without iterative scans or other filtering strategies.
Horizontal scaling, sharding, managed hosting, replication, security, and backup behavior depend on PostgreSQL and the selected deployment ecosystem rather than pgvector alone.
Hybrid search composition and score fusion are not a single built-in pgvector operation and require SQL or application logic.
usageGuidance: Record the installed extension version and PostgreSQL version because supported features and limits evolve.
Use EXPLAIN with ANALYZE and BUFFERS to inspect query plans and verify that the intended scalar or vector index is used.
Monitor recall by comparing approximate searches with exact search on representative queries.
Use transaction-local search parameters when tuning a specific query without changing the session default.

references.title: pgvector: Open-source vector similarity search for Postgres

claims.statement: pgvector performs exact nearest-neighbor search by default and supports approximate nearest-neighbor search with HNSW and IVFFlat indexes.
claims.rationale: The official project README distinguishes exact search from the HNSW and IVFFlat approximate index types.

claims.statement: pgvector documents Euclidean, inner-product, cosine, L1, Hamming, and Jaccard distance operations, with index support depending on the vector representation and index method.
claims.rationale: The official README lists operators and operator classes for dense, half-precision, sparse, and binary vector types.

claims.statement: For approximate vector indexes, filtering is applied after the index scan by default; pgvector documents iterative scans, partial indexes, and partitioning as mitigation strategies.

qualifiers.name: queryScope
qualifiers.value: Approximate HNSW and IVFFlat retrieval with SQL predicates

claims.rationale: The filtering section of the official README explicitly describes post-scan filtering and documented alternatives.

claims.statement: pgvector can be combined with PostgreSQL full-text search for hybrid retrieval, with Reciprocal Rank Fusion or a cross-encoder used to combine or rerank result sets.

qualifiers.name: implementationScope
qualifiers.value: SQL and application-level hybrid retrieval composition

claims.rationale: The pgvector README recommends PostgreSQL full-text search and names Reciprocal Rank Fusion and cross-encoder combination.

claims.statement: Because pgvector is a PostgreSQL extension, vector data operations participate in PostgreSQL transaction semantics; pgvector also documents transaction-local tuning for HNSW and IVFFlat search parameters.

qualifiers.name: hostDependency
qualifiers.value: Transaction guarantees are provided by PostgreSQL

claims.rationale: PostgreSQL documents transaction isolation while pgvector shows SET LOCAL search tuning inside explicit transactions.

evidence.summary: The official pgvector README states that exact search is the default and lists HNSW and IVFFlat as approximate index types.
evidence.interpretation: This directly supports modeling pgvector with Flat, HNSW, and IVF Flat retrieval/index approaches.
limitations: Project documentation is authoritative for capabilities but is not an independent benchmark.
Approximate-index performance depends on data, hardware, parameters, and PostgreSQL configuration.

evidence.summary: The official reference documents L2, inner-product, cosine, L1, Hamming, and Jaccard operations across supported vector types.
evidence.interpretation: The RKM distance-metric profile can conservatively include the six corresponding schema values.

sourceFragments.locator: README sections: HNSW, IVFFlat, Binary Vectors, Sparse Vectors, Reference

limitations: Not every distance metric is indexable for every vector type or index method.
Supported dimensions and operator behavior are version-specific.

evidence.summary: The README explains that approximate-index filters are applied after scanning and documents iterative scans, partial indexes, and partitioning.
evidence.interpretation: pgvector supports filtered retrieval, but its filtering profile must retain planner- and index-dependent limitations.

sourceFragments.locator: README sections: Filtering, Iterative Index Scans

limitations: The PostgreSQL planner may choose a table scan, scalar index, or vector index.
Filtering with approximate indexes can return fewer rows without sufficient scan parameters.

evidence.summary: The pgvector README recommends PostgreSQL full-text search for hybrid search and mentions RRF or a cross-encoder; PostgreSQL documents its full-text search subsystem.
evidence.interpretation: Hybrid retrieval is supported through composition, not through a single pgvector-native end-to-end hybrid operator.

sourceFragments.locator: PostgreSQL documentation: Chapter 12 Full Text Search

limitations: RRF, score fusion, or cross-encoder reranking must be designed in SQL or application logic.
The sources do not establish a universal best fusion method.

evidence.summary: PostgreSQL documents transaction isolation levels and pgvector shows HNSW and IVFFlat search parameters set locally within a transaction.
evidence.interpretation: The model can record Full ACID transaction support while clearly attributing those guarantees to the PostgreSQL host.

sourceFragments.locator: README sections: HNSW Query Options, IVFFlat Query Options

limitations: Transaction guarantees come from PostgreSQL rather than a separate pgvector transaction layer.
Read-replica freshness and distributed consistency depend on deployment architecture.
